newsitem.title: HAITI: Former Haitian president denounces government.
newsitem.headline: Former Haitian president denounces government.

text.p: Former Haitian president Jean-Bertrand Aristide has denounced Haiti's current president, Rene Preval, for supporting a U.S.-backed programme to overhaul the nation's economy.
In remarks broadcast on Monday, Aristide said the programme, which includes lowering taxes on imports, benefits the rich at the expense of Haiti's impoverished majority.

"It is a game of organising their own business rules which are good for those that have more, and bad for those that have less. For (the international community) it is them first, them next, and them in the end," he said in his strongest criticism yet of the programme.
Aristide's remarks, made on Saturday at his Aristide Foundation for Democracy, were broadcast for the first time on Monday.

Preval began his political career as a protege of Aristide, a charismatic former priest considered a hero by Haiti's impoverished masses. But a rift grew between the two after Preval succeeded Aristide as Haiti's president. Aristide has since formed his own political party, Fanmi Lavalas, breaking with Preval's Lavalas Political Organisation.
Preval has said the economic reform plan is the only solution for Haiti, the poorest country in the Western hemisphere.

But candidates from Aristide's party won both the seats decided during the most recent parliamentary elections in April, and were expected to take the remaining 7 seats out of the 27 in Haiti's Senate to be decided in a runoff set for June 15.
